derivations.method: Report time is printed (20:20 JFK local / 00:20Z), so the instant was read, not computed; what I derived is its calendar date. to_utc places JFK 2026-09-16T20:20 at 2026-09-17T00:20Z, so the report belongs to 17 Sep UTC even though the row is dated 16SEP. Cross-checked against the sector: STD 01:50Z on 17 Sep is 90 minutes later, consistent with the same offset seen on every other flight row.

Same situation in reverse: report prints 00:25 LHR local / 23:25Z, and to_utc places LHR 2026-09-27T00:25 at 2026-09-26T23:25Z. The report instant therefore falls on 26 Sep UTC, one hour before the 00:25Z departure on 27 Sep.

Off duty prints '01:20/00:20Z+1'. The +1 belongs to the local column (21SEP 01:20 LHR), and to_utc confirms LHR 2026-09-21T00:50 = 2026-09-20T23:50Z for the STA, so the printed Z values are 20 Sep for arrival and 21 Sep 00:20Z for off duty. Sanity-checked by block time: 10:30Z to 23:50Z is 13h20, matching the outbound LHR-SIN on 18SEP.

SIM row has no STD, so report is the printed start of the training window (08:00 LHR local / 07:00Z) taken with no reporting offset, per the rule that training report is the stated venue start time. End 16:00/15:00Z read from the Off Duty column.
